_golden.type: one case for each presence form: the visible range (viewport in cells), the cell caret, a range as one unit, and claims on ranges; with their wire frames and roster events. r1: an agent's cells after each kind of verb (AG1-AG4), sheet states (HS1), width and height units (UN1)
notes: r1.1: CS8, CS9, CS11 and CC2 are real frames (ops_change, presence_refused, roster events, ErrorReports), on branches from rev 20; AG3 skips hidden rows; ST1 is new
r1: the sample now has two hidden sheets (Lists, sheetId 3, hidden; Setup, sheetId 4, very hidden), so the sheet the turn adds is @sheet:5
state: keyed-state-rev20.json unless a case says otherwise. Row addresses name keys, not row numbers
MARKS: 'EXISTS' = on kit main 44c3c9ff; 'NEW' = asked by this addendum, not built

the frame type 'cells', the roster kind 'cells', the feature 'cells', the claim frame's 'cells' field and the roster kind 'claim_started_cells' are NEW names, proposed here; the kit picks the final spelling at its WIRE bump

a corner is {row, row_off, col, col_off}: the last keyed row (column) at or before the cell, then an offset. The kit refuses a corner that isn't in this form (MPC-E114), so two clients never spell one cell two ways
_a1 fields are annotations, not on the wire

cases.form: focus moves to another sheet
cases.means: a PERSON's cells value is dropped (roster event cells: null in the same flush as the focus). See VR4 and presence-and-claims.json P3 (Ada). An agent's cells after a verb follow AG1-AG4 instead (r1)

cases.form: an agent's cells after a verb that writes cells (r1 ruling 1)
cases.rule: the frame's derived 'written' (the pack's rectangles, by corners at the frame's rev) becomes the agent's cells: ranges = written, active = the first range's start
cases.example: turn-frames.json rev 21: written D5:D7, then cells {active D5, ranges [D5:D7]} in the same flush

cases.form: after an insert (r1 ruling 2)
cases.rule: the inserted rows or columns, as whole-band ranges (a row band runs to column 16,384; a column band to row 1,048,576); active = the band's start
cases.example: rev 23: rows insert at 10, cells {active A10, ranges [A10:XFD10]}, which is also its 'written'

cases.form: after a delete (r1 ruling 2; r1.1: visible cells only)
cases.rule: a caret on the first VISIBLE cell after the deleted band. For rows: the first row after it that isn't hidden, in the first column that isn't hidden. For columns: the first visible column after it, in the first visible row. No ranges. If nothing visible follows, the last visible cell before the band. The frame has no 'written'; its 'bands' names the deleted band by its numbers before the change
cases.example: rev 28: blank row 17 deleted. Row 17 is now the hidden fx row, so the caret skips it: A18 = {row: @sheet:1/row:r16, row_off: 0, col: @sheet:1/col:c1, col_off: 0}. CS8 has a delete with no hidden row after it (A14)

cases.form: after a sheet add or rename (r1 ruling 2)
cases.rule: focus moves to that sheet. The agent's cells are kept if they are on that sheet, else they become a caret at A1 of it

examples._a1: A1 of an empty sheet: no keyed row or column yet

cases.form: sheet states in the index (r1 ruling 6)
cases.means: hidden stays a bool for every view; state tells a view which hidden sheets the file hides from its own menus ('hidden by the file', Q-X14). From the sheet's state field: visible, hidden, veryHidden

cases.form: widths and heights (r1 ruling 8)
cases.mark: NEW (names only; the values EXIST in the store)

column_width.unit: characters of the default font's maximum digit width, as stored in the file

cases.means: the grid slot names both units. Pixels are K2's: points × 96 / 72 for heights; for widths, the default font's maximum digit width in pixels, which needs that font's metrics (HYPOTHESIS: the pack can derive the default font's name and size from the carrier's styles part, for K2 to measure)

cases.form: a missing style table or style index (r1.1)
cases.rule: a cell whose sheet has no 'styles' table, or whose style index isn't in it, takes the default style: {bold: false, fill: null, numfmt: 'General'}. Never an error, never a guess from another sheet's table
cases.golden: Notes (@sheet:5) is added at rev 27 with no derived.styles at all: its frame's derived is null. A cell written there before the pack sends a table shows unbold, unfilled, General
cases.and: a cell whose register says s 3 on a sheet whose table lacks '3' shows the default too, until a frame's derived.containers brings the sheet's table. A pack sends the table when a write uses a style index the sheet's table lacks (recommended)
